newsitem.title: USA: Selfix sees FY '96 net at $0.05-0.07/shr.
newsitem.headline: Selfix sees FY '96 net at $0.05-0.07/shr.

text.p: Selfix Inc, which is returning to profitability following a restructuring, said Tuesday it expects "to be solidly in the black" for all of 1996, with earnings estimated at $0.05 to $0.07 a share.
Selfix, which makes and markets home accessories, also said it expects to "have substantially improved net earnings for 1997 in the $0.30 to $0.40 range."
Net sales for third quarter ended September 28, 1996, increased 3.9 percent to $10.7 million from $10.3 million a year earlier. EPS climbed to $0.20 from $0.01.
Per-share earnings for the first nine months of 1996 totaled $0.09 compared with a loss of $0.05 a year ago.
Results benefited from an improved product mix and lower expenses, Chairman James Tennant said in a statement.

He said that as a result of cost-cutting efforts and improved product mix, the company's housewares business has reduced its break-even sales point by more than $6 million in 1996 to about $31 million from 1995's $39 million and 1994's $41 million. The company expects the break-even level to decline by another $2 million in 1997 to the range of $29 million, he said.
Shares of Selfix were trading off 3/8 to 4-3/8.
